newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai oil, gas demand up 9.1 pct in Jan-July.
newsitem.headline: Thai oil, gas demand up 9.1 pct in Jan-July.

text.p: Thai oil and natural gas consumption rose 9.1 percent year-on-year to the equivalent of 882,590 barrels per day (bpd) in the first seven months of this year, the Petroleum Authority of Thailand (PTT) said on Monday.
It said consumption of refined oil products averaged 730,220 bpd from January to July, up 9.5 percent from the same period last year.
Consumption of natural gas was 152,370 barrels of oil equivalent per day, a 7.5 percent rise.
Oil imports in the first seven months averaged 772,460 bpd, up 19.5 percent from the same period last year.
Refined oil product imports were 181,570 bpd, down 7.5 percent, and crude product imports were 590,890 bpd, up 31.4 percent, the PTT said.
Of the crude imports, 406,310 bpd were from the Middle East, a 40.9 percent increase over the same period last year. Imports from the Far East amounted to 171,110 bpd, a 9.3 percent rise.

The value crude imports in the first seven months totalled 61.57 billion baht ($2.46 billion), up 45.7 percent over last year. The total value of refined oil imports amounted to 22.1 billion baht, up 4.8 percent.
